source_detail: Built in ca-tools 2026-11-11 in four steps, all run by programs/recipe.sh. Step 1, profile product (method of Colbourn and Torres-Jimenez 2013, Thm 4.2 / Cor 4.5, programs/pprod.py) of our CA(17; 2, 29, 3) (programs/CA_17_2_29_3_16af2149.txt, built 2026-10-30 by simulated annealing with column extension from a random start, rows 7 and 16, which agree in 6 columns) with the orthogonal array OA(9, 4, 3) with rows (i, j, i+j, i+2j) mod 3 (rows 0 and 1, which agree in 1 column). The product has 17 + 9 - 3 = 23 rows and 29 x 4 - 6 x 1 = 110 columns. No search in this step. Step 2, column extension with programs/ext2t.c, one column at a time, with the 8 rows that come from the orthogonal array free to change together with the new column (simulated annealing with exact pair counts, temperature 0.65, seed 2003, each new column the best of 200 random columns, a stuck column redrawn after 200000 moves). The array saved at 136 columns (move 402,147,672) is kept. Step 3, the same program with all 23 rows free (temperature 0.40, seed 2003). The array saved at 137 columns (move 12,900,846) is kept. Step 4, exact, programs/drop1.c: for each column in turn, remove it and list every column that is qualitatively independent of all 136 remaining columns. With column 48 removed (counting from 0) there are exactly 3 such columns and two of them are qualitatively independent of each other. The array is the 136 remaining columns followed by those two. Exact check with ca_verify, all column pairs
construction: Profile product of an own CA(17; 2, 29, 3) with OA(9, 4, 3), CA(23; 2, 110, 3), then column extension by simulated annealing to 137 columns, then one column replaced by two after an exhaustive list of the columns that fit
notes: ties the cited size 23 rows at 138 columns; no Torres-Jimenez array is an ingredient or start; the programs were written by AI models for this project
